8 candidate TBC systems were evaluated, consisting of 1 bond coat alloy (Ni-22Cr-10Al-1Y) and 4 ceramic top coat materials (Al2O3, Zr02-20%Y203, Zr02-24%MgO, HfO2).

The Zr02-20%Y203 top coat was selected based on results from metallography, X-ray diffraction, tensile bond testing, bend testing, erosion testing, thermal cycling, furnace exposure, and high velocity dynamic oxidation testing.
Procedures were developed for applying the Ni-Cr-Al-Y bond coat by vacuum plasma spraying and the Zr02-20%Y203 top coat by atmospheric plasma spraying on CF6-50 turbine blades and vanes.
In the cascade rig test, the TBC on the Stage 1 blades was in good condition even in areas adjacent to local melting of the substrate.
Component high cycle fatigue testing at 1200K showed the TBC-coated Stage 2 blades had comparable strength to uncoated blades.
In the first engine test, the TBC-coated blades were severely damaged by an unrelated engine failure, but the bond coat remained intact over most of the airfoil.
In the second engine test with 1000 cycles, the TBC on the Stage 2 blades was in excellent condition except for some coating loss at the leading edge above midspan on the suction side.
Some coating loss occurred from the outer 1/3 to 2/3 of the vane leading edges, likely due to thermal spalling, and localized erosion was seen on the outer band near the leading edge.
The TBC did not significantly degrade the high cycle fatigue, low cycle fatigue, or stress rupture properties of the Rene 80, Rene 150, and X-40 substrate alloys.
